title: Peacepunck (West Branch of Nissequogue River)
summary: Peacepunck names the west branch of the Nissequogue River in Smithtown, where a partition division among Richard Smith's heirs described a branch south of the mills.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Nissequogue River near Smithtown / New Mill Pond landscape point based on Tooker location; not an exact colonial branch or mill coordinate.
history_content: The placename belongs to the river-branch and mill landscape in Smithtown. Partition and etymology details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
The history cross-references Pesapunck, where the related meaning is a hot house or sweat lodge. The exact relationship between the Smithtown branch name and the later Pesapunck entry remains uncertain.

Why Place Names Matter

“The name given to a place or site on the land often describes what is special or important about that place.”

— Michael Heine, Alestine Andre, Ingrid Kritsch, Alma Cardinal, and the Elders of Tsiigehtshik, Gwichya Gwich'in Googwandak: The History and Stories of the Gwichya Gwich'in As Told by the Elders of Tsiigehtshik (2007), PDF page 55, The Many Meanings of Names and Stories
whereintheworld_content: Approximate/general point near the Nissequogue River west-branch and mill-pond landscape southwest of Smithtown. This is not an exact colonial branch, mill, or partition-boundary coordinate.
